scenes.headline: The warning that never appeared
scenes.body: Patched, but only if you update.
scenes.say: Windows users: that download warning may never appear. Here's why.

scenes.headline: Downloads get a hidden internet tag
scenes.body: It's called Mark of the Web. It triggers the warnings.
scenes.say: When you download a file, Windows quietly marks it as coming from the internet. That tag, called Mark of the Web, is what triggers the warnings.

scenes.headline: A crafted file slips past the tag
scenes.body: CVE-2026-96951 in Windows Shell. No warning, no Protected View.
scenes.say: A flaw in Windows Shell lets a specially crafted file slip past that tag. No warning. No Protected View.

scenes.headline: out of 10
scenes.body: Microsoft confirmed it is being exploited
scenes.say: Microsoft rates it eight point eight out of ten, and confirmed attackers are already exploiting it.

scenes.headline: Fixed, then flagged

items.text: Microsoft fix ships; CISA lists it as exploited
Patch deadline for US federal agencies

scenes.say: Microsoft fixed it on October thirteenth, and the US agency CISA listed it as exploited the same day. Federal agencies had until October sixteenth to patch.

scenes.headline: No warning doesn't mean safe.
scenes.body: This attack still needs you to open the file.
scenes.say: Analyst note: no warning doesn't mean a file is safe. This attack still needs you to open it.

scenes.headline: Do this tonight
scenes.say: Tonight: open Settings, then Windows Update. Install everything and restart. And if a file arrives unexpectedly, don't open it.

scenes.headline: The security story behind the headline.
scenes.say: Sources are in the description. Follow Securidge.
